syllabus_topics: Introduction to Industrial Automation: industrial automation pyramid
Elements of combinatorial and sequential logic
Grafcet standard for representing sequential system models
Architecture and programming languages of programmable logic controllers
Applications of Grafcet models to industrial controller programming
Pneumatic and hydraulic actuation systems
Dynamic models of discrete events
Finite state machines
Relationship between Grafcet models and finite state machines
Composition of finite state machines
Petri nets
Analysis of Petri nets
Applications of Petri nets
Fundamentals of digital communication and digital networks
Synchronous and asynchronous communication between elements: same hierarchical level and different levels
Isochronous communication between sensors, actuators and controllers
Industrial communication protocols
Automatically guided vehicles
Communication between programmable logic controllers and industrial devices
Safety standards and analysis
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.5 * Exam Grade + 0.5 * Laboratory Grade. The Laboratory Grade is 0.30 * Lab1 + 0.35 * Lab2 + 0.35 * Lab3. A minimum of 8.0 out of 20 is required for the Exam Grade and 9.5 out of 20 for the Laboratory Grade. Students with a Final Grade > 18 may be required to take an oral confirmation exam or accept a final grade of 18. Student workers can opt to perform laboratory work individually by prior arrangement; their absence from a lab work implies a score of 0, and laboratory assessments are not subject to appeal. Special examination period rules are the same as regular and resit periods, with the lab component fulfilled by an individual project.
